note: **Jurisdiction note:** Deposit limits (e.g. maximum months' rent) often vary by local law. This often depends on local law; ask a local lawyer what the permitted deposit cap is in your area.

**Jurisdiction note:** Minimum notice periods for tenancy termination or eviction are frequently set by local tenancy law and may override what the agreement says. Ask a local lawyer about the statutory minimum in your jurisdiction.
**Jurisdiction note:** Rent increase caps (rent control / rent stabilisation) vary widely by city and state. This often depends on local law; ask a local lawyer whether a cap applies to your tenancy.

**Jurisdiction note:** Requirements for registering a lease or paying stamp duty differ by state and lease duration. This often depends on local law; ask a local lawyer or sub-registrar's office what applies in your area.

**Jurisdiction note:** The enforceability of non-compete and non-solicitation clauses varies significantly by jurisdiction and may be limited or unenforceable in some places. Ask a local lawyer before signing.
**Jurisdiction note:** Maximum permissible interest rates on arrears or penalties are often regulated by local law. This often depends on local law; ask a local lawyer what the applicable limit is.

**Jurisdiction note:** Arbitration clauses may have seat, rules and enforceability implications that depend on the governing law and location of the parties. Ask a local lawyer whether the agreed arbitration forum applies to you.

**Jurisdiction note:** Statutory notice pay, severance entitlements and grounds for dismissal are regulated differently in each jurisdiction. This often depends on local law; ask a local labour lawyer what minimum protections apply.
